title: Complement Workup: Pathways, CH50/AH50 Patterns and Hereditary Angioedema
summary: Map the classical, lectin and alternative pathways onto the shared terminal pathway, use CH50 and AH50 together to localize a deficiency, link terminal gaps to Neisseria, and test for hereditary angioedema.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 48 Hits 1, 2, 5, 6, 8 and 11 and Trap 3 (first lesson for Ch. 48). Checked against Merle 2015, Al-Shaikhly 2020, Blazina 2018 and the WAO/EAACI 2021 HAE guideline. The AH50-only row (factor B, D, properdin) is derived from the pathway map, not from a cited case. Not taught as fact: sheep/rabbit erythrocyte assay details, IgG4 not activating C1, SLE C3/C4 activity patterns, HAE type-specific numeric cut-offs and attack duration, C3 nephritic factor, PNH details, MBL figures, carboxypeptidase N, classical-vs-alternative consumption patterns (Hits 3–4, 7, 9–10, 12–14).

objectives: Name the C3 convertases of the classical/lectin and alternative pathways and the components of the MAC.
Use CH50 and AH50 results together to localize a complement deficiency.
Link terminal-component deficiency to Neisseria infection and choose tests for hereditary angioedema.

scenes.title: A second meningococcal infection
scenes.altText: Invented case: a 16-year-old is admitted with Neisseria meningitidis meningitis for the second time. The clinician sends complement screening: CH50 UNDETECTABLE; AH50 result pending. Question token: “Which piece of complement is missing — and what does the second test add?”

cues.text: A 16-year-old has meningococcal meningitis for the second time.
Complement screening comes back: CH50 is undetectable. The AH50 is still pending.
Which piece of complement is missing, and what will the second test add?

scenes.title: Three on-ramps, one highway
scenes.altText: Schematic map (Merle 2015). Classical pathway: C1q (with C1r₂C1s₂) recognizes targets such as antibody clusters; lectin pathway: MBL or ficolins with MASPs. Both cleave C4 and C2 (Ca²⁺ needed) → C4b2a = the classical/lectin C3 convertase. Alternative pathway: constant low-level “tick-over” of C3 to C3(H₂O); factor D cleaves factor B bound to C3b → C3bBb = the alternative C3 convertase; properdin helps recruit C3b to surfaces. Shared highway: C3 → C3a (inflammation) + C3b (opsonin); C3b joins the convertase to form a C5 convertase → C5a + C5b; C5b recruits C6, C7, C8 and C9, which polymerizes into the membrane attack complex (MAC) pore; host cells resist via CD59.

cues.text: Complement has three on-ramps. The classical pathway starts when C1q binds targets such as antibody clusters; the lectin pathway starts with MBL or ficolins.
Both cleave C4 and C2 to build C4b2a, the classical and lectin C3 convertase.
The alternative pathway idles all the time. Factor D cuts factor B bound to C3b, making C3bBb, the alternative C3 convertase. Properdin helps it form on surfaces.
All roads meet at C3. C3b builds a C5 convertase; C5b then gathers C6, C7, C8 and many C9 molecules into the membrane attack complex, a pore that lyses targets.

props.title: Shared terminal highway
lines: C5b + C6 + C7 + C8 + C9 → MAC pore

scenes.title: What a missing piece does
scenes.altText: Case cards (Al-Shaikhly 2020, pediatric cohort; functional CH50/AH50 by hemolytic assays): C2 deficiency — CH50 undetectable, C2 low; pneumococcal and streptococcal infections. C1q deficiency — CH50 undetectable, AH50 NORMAL. C6 deficiency — CH50 undetectable; N. meningitidis meningitis. C8 deficiency — CH50 low and AH50 UNDETECTABLE; two episodes of meningococcal meningitis. Blazina 2018: AH50 is not affected by C2 deficiency; complement activity is routinely measured after a first N. meningitidis infection; homozygous C1–C9 defects lead to recurrent infections with encapsulated bacteria and autoimmune phenomena.

cues.text: Real cases show the logic. Children missing C2 or C1q had an undetectable CH50, and the C1q-deficient child had a normal AH50.
Those early classical defects came with pneumococcal and streptococcal infections.
Children missing C6 or C8, parts of the shared membrane attack complex, had meningococcal meningitis. The C8-deficient patient had a low CH50 and an undetectable AH50.
So an early classical gap knocks out only CH50, while a gap on the shared highway knocks out both tests. That is why complement is checked after a first meningococcal infection.

props.label: Early gap → CH50 only · highway gap → both

scenes.title: Localize, confirm, and test for HAE
scenes.altText: Pattern table (logic from the pathway map, Merle 2015; consistent with the case series): CH50 ↓, AH50 normal → C1q/C1r/C1s, C4 or C2; CH50 ↓ and AH50 ↓ → C3 or C5–C9; AH50 ↓, CH50 normal → an alternative-pathway-only factor (factor B, factor D or properdin). Then measure individual components (level and function). Handling token (Blazina 2018): improper sample handling during transport can activate complement in vitro and limit evaluation. HAE card (WAO/EAACI 2021): HAE-1 = C1-inhibitor deficiency; HAE-2 = dysfunctional C1-inhibitor; both cause bradykinin overproduction → angioedema; autosomal dominant (SERPING1), ~1 in 50,000; diagnose with C1-INH function, C1-INH protein AND C4 together. Hook answer: an AH50 that is also undetectable points to the shared terminal pathway (e.g. C5–C9).

cues.text: Put the two screens together. CH50 low with a normal AH50 points to an early classical component: C1, C4 or C2. Both low points to C3 or the terminal components.
AH50 low with a normal CH50 points to an alternative-only factor such as factor B, factor D or properdin. Then confirm by measuring individual components.
Handle samples carefully: complement activated in the tube can look like a deficiency.

Hereditary angioedema is a different question: C1 inhibitor is missing in type 1 or faulty in type 2, and bradykinin causes the swelling. Test C1 inhibitor function, C1 inhibitor protein and C4 together.
For our patient, if the AH50 is also undetectable, the gap is on the shared terminal highway, such as C5 to C9.

props.title: CH50 / AH50 pattern
lines: CH50 ↓ · AH50 nl → C1, C4, C2
AH50 ↓ · CH50 nl → B, D, properdin

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “An undetectable CH50 means the alternative pathway is broken too” (✓ CH50 tests classical + terminal; a normal AH50 localizes the gap to C1, C4 or C2); “HAE type 2 has low C1-inhibitor protein” (✓ type 2 = dysfunctional C1-INH — measure FUNCTION, protein and C4); “Hereditary angioedema is histamine-mediated like allergy” (✓ bradykinin overproduction).

cues.text: Trap one: an undetectable CH50 means the alternative pathway is broken too. No: CH50 tests the classical pathway. If AH50 is normal, the gap is C1, C4 or C2.
Trap two: type 2 hereditary angioedema has low C1 inhibitor protein. No: in type 2 the inhibitor is dysfunctional, so measure its function as well as protein and C4.
Trap three: hereditary angioedema is histamine-mediated, like allergy. No: the swelling comes from overproduction of bradykinin.

props.title: ✗ “CH50 = 0 → alternative broken too.”
lines: ✓ Check AH50: normal → C1, C4 or C2

scenes.title: On-ramps and the highway
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “CH50 drives the Classical on-ramp onto the highway; AH50 drives the Alternative on-ramp onto the same highway. One car stalls → its on-ramp is blocked. Both stall → the highway (C3, C5–C9) is closed.” Tokens: CH50 = classical + terminal · AH50 = alternative + terminal · both ↓ = C3/C5–C9. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: CH50 drives the classical on-ramp onto the highway; AH50 drives the alternative on-ramp onto the same highway. If one car stalls, its on-ramp is blocked; if both stall, the highway itself is closed.

Where it breaks: a partial deficiency lowers rather than zeroes the result; complement activated in the tube, or consumed in active disease such as lupus, can stall both cars without any inherited gap; and C1-inhibitor problems are not detected this way.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: C1-INH defects need their own tests

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “CH50 ↓ AH50 nl → C1/C4/C2 · both ↓ → C3 or C5–C9 · AH50 ↓ only → B/D/properdin”, “Terminal gaps → Neisseria · HAE-1/2: C1-INH function + protein + C4 (bradykinin)”.

cues.text: Reading CH50 and AH50 together localizes a complement gap, with both undetectable pointing to C3 or the terminal components that protect against Neisseria, while hereditary angioedema needs C1-inhibitor function, protein and C4.

props.label: CH50↓ AH50 nl → C1/C4/C2 · both ↓ → C3/C5–C9 · AH50↓ → B/D/P
Terminal gaps → Neisseria · HAE: C1-INH function + protein + C4

explanation.what: Plain language: complement is a cascade with three entry routes that merge into one shared end route that punches holes in microbes; two screening tests each drive one entry route down the shared end route, so which test fails tells you where the break is. Scientific terms: classical, lectin and alternative pathways, C1q, MBL, MASPs, C3 convertase (C4b2a, C3bBb), factor B, factor D, properdin, C5 convertase, membrane attack complex (C5b-9), CH50, AH50, C1-inhibitor, bradykinin.
explanation.why: CH50 needs every classical and terminal component; AH50 needs every alternative and terminal component. A missing early classical protein stops only CH50; a missing C3 or terminal protein stops both. Without the MAC, Neisseria are poorly killed. C1-inhibitor loss lets bradykinin build up.
explanation.measure: Hemolytic CH50 and AH50 screens; pattern localizes the gap; confirm with individual component levels/function (Al-Shaikhly 2020; Blazina 2018). Avoid in-vitro activation from poor handling. HAE-1/2: C1-INH function, C1-INH protein and C4 together (WAO/EAACI 2021).
explanation.differs: Early classical deficiency (CH50 ↓, AH50 normal; encapsulated bacteria) vs terminal deficiency (both ↓; Neisseria); HAE-1 (deficient C1-INH) vs HAE-2 (dysfunctional C1-INH).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: localize a deficiency from CH50/AH50, link recurrent Neisseria to C5–C9, and choose C1-INH function/protein plus C4 for suspected HAE.

mnemonic.text: CH50 drives the Classical on-ramp onto the highway; AH50 drives the Alternative on-ramp onto the same highway. One car stalls → its on-ramp is blocked. Both stall → the highway (C3, C5–C9) is closed.
mnemonic.explanation: Each screen tests one entry pathway plus the shared terminal pathway.
mnemonic.limitation: Partial deficiencies lower rather than zero results; in-vitro activation or consumption can stall both; C1-INH defects need their own tests.

questions.stem: A child with recurrent pneumococcal infections has an undetectable CH50 and a normal AH50. Which component is most likely deficient?

options.rationale: Correct. An early classical component; AH50 does not need C2, so it stays normal.
Incorrect. A terminal component; both CH50 and AH50 would be abnormal.
Incorrect. C3 is shared, so AH50 would also be abnormal.
Incorrect. Factor B is alternative-only; AH50 would be low and CH50 normal.

questions.stem: A young adult has a second episode of meningococcal meningitis. CH50 and AH50 are both undetectable. Which deficiency fits best?

options.rationale: Correct. Both screens need the shared terminal pathway, and terminal deficiencies are linked to Neisseria infection.
Incorrect. C1q deficiency leaves AH50 normal.
Incorrect. C1-INH deficiency causes hereditary angioedema, not absent CH50/AH50.
Incorrect. An alternative-only defect would leave CH50 normal.

questions.stem: Recurrent non-itchy swelling without hives suggests hereditary angioedema. Which test combination does the WAO/EAACI guideline use?

options.text: C1-inhibitor function, C1-inhibitor protein and C4
options.rationale: Correct. The combination is more accurate than any one test and detects both type 1 and type 2.
Incorrect. These address mast-cell/allergic causes; HAE is bradykinin-mediated.
Incorrect. Type 2 has dysfunctional inhibitor; protein alone can miss it.
Incorrect. AH50 screens the alternative pathway, not C1-inhibitor.
